name: perf-pass
summary: Performance measured in parts: test rooms that find first-use hitches per effect or actor by name, fly-bys for what the level costs, and labelled play runs; plus the prewarm that ships in the game so anything spawned during play appears instantly.

MODULE.description: The C++ game module the two source files join (the directory under Source/).

MODULE_API.description: That module's export macro, for example MYGAME_API.

adapt: Add "Niagara", "Json", "RenderCore" and "RHI" to PublicDependencyModuleNames in Source/<Module>/<Module>.Build.cs.
Close the editor, then compile: node Tools/gam3/ue_build.mjs

Copy Tools/gam3/perf.example.json to Tools/gam3/perf.json. List under room.subjects every effect, actor class, mesh and material the game spawns during play, and under flyby.points a route through each level.

For every subject the room reports as a first-use hitch, add it to Assets under [/Script/<Module>.Gam3Prewarm] in Config/DefaultGame.ini (or call UGam3Prewarm::Warm from the game mode's BeginPlay), then prove it with --prewarm.
Call UGam3PerfProbe::Mark(this, "wave 3") where the game changes what it is doing, so a play run reports by name.

verified.how: Compiled into a fresh C++ project with ready-gate. Room with the engine's default Niagara system and a cube: the cold run failed the Niagara system by name (first ever run 2.0 s of load, later runs about 210 ms of load plus a 12 ms first-draw spike against 9 ms warm) and passed the cube; with --prewarm, and separately with the system listed under Gam3Prewarm in DefaultGame.ini, load was 0 ms, first use matched warm and the run passed. Fly-by over three points on a landscape level wrote one segment per leg. Play with a scratch subsystem calling Mark wrote both labels. A baseline was saved and an identical run compared ok; a run with 6 ms of busy work added per frame was reported regressed (game thread 0.7 to 6.6 ms). Those ran with --shared while other engines were running. Alone on the machine (the default, which held every engine slot): the room gave the same verdicts, and a 15 s play run driven by the walk-bot kit (--bot wander) measured 1800 frames with the bot's summary printed. Windowed runs on this Mac were locked to the 120 Hz display, which the tool reported; the render thread's own cost could not be read. Not run: a packaged or Shipping build, the game's prewarm in a packaged build, actor-class, skeletal-mesh and material subjects, World Partition streaming during a fly-by, Windows and Linux. 0.2.0: no Blueprint exposure; actor-class subjects are named by script path and a Blueprint asset path is no longer resolved; the summary reports machine_load and warns when other work on the machine makes the numbers untrustworthy (seen once, when an unrelated build pushed a room run to 76 ms a frame). Recompiled; the prewarmed room ran. 0.3.0: hitches name their cause and subjects report pipeline states and packages on first use (an effect's first use listed 64 packages and the pipeline states created). Cascade particle systems are spawned by name. The prewarm waits until no new pipeline state appears, and the room is lit before the prewarm. Run in a real game on five Cascade effects, four skeletal meshes, a static mesh and two materials: first-use pipeline states fell from 73 cold to 21 prewarmed. The machine was busy with unrelated work for every run in that game, which the tool reported, so no frame-time number from it is recorded here.
